# Fleet Bundle

Generated by AICR v1.0.0

## Prerequisites

- Rancher with Fleet (HelmOps and GitRepos are part of every Rancher install)
- `kubectl` configured for the Rancher management (local) cluster
- A Git repository Fleet can read

## Bundles

Fleet reconciles the bundles in this order; each one `dependsOn` the previous
bundle and starts only after it is `Ready`.

| Bundle | Release | Namespace | Version |
|--------|---------|-----------|---------|
| aicr-cert-manager | cert-manager | cert-manager | v1.17.2 |

## Deployment

1. Push this directory to the repository and branch named in `gitrepo.yaml`
   (edit `spec.repo` / `spec.branch` if you did not pass `--repo`). If the
   bundle lives in a subdirectory of the repository, prefix every entry in
   `spec.paths` with that subdirectory.

2. Apply the GitRepo to the Fleet workspace `fleet-default`:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f gitrepo.yaml
   ```

3. Opt clusters in. Nothing is deployed until a cluster carries the label
   the GitRepo selects on:

   ```bash
   kubectl label clusters.fleet.cattle.io -n fleet-default <cluster> aicr.nvidia.com/bundle=aicr
   ```

Monitor progress in Rancher under **Continuous Delivery**, or:

```bash
kubectl get bundles -n fleet-default -l aicr.nvidia.com/bundle=aicr
```

If a release with the same name already exists in the target namespace (for
example a GPU Operator installed with `helm install gpu-operator`), Fleet
upgrades it in place. Objects owned by a release with a different name are
not adopted: the install fails on the ownership conflict instead, so remove
or rename that release first.

### Per-cluster customization

Releases with dynamic value paths have a `cluster-values.yaml` next to
`values.yaml`; edit it before pushing. To vary values per cluster, add
`targetCustomizations` to that folder's `fleet.yaml`.

## Removal

```bash
kubectl delete -f gitrepo.yaml
```

Fleet uninstalls every release in the bundle.

## Limitations

- Fleet installs charts with Helm, which creates a chart's `crds/` on first
  install but never upgrades them.
- Readiness hooks (`--readiness-hooks`) are not supported.
- A chart that ships CRDs in `crds/`, templates objects of those kinds, and
  uses Helm `lookup` fails Fleet's server-side dry run on a cluster where the
  CRDs do not exist yet. Apply that chart's CRDs first.
